author: Radde, 1863
summary: 저수지와 강, 강 하구에서 주로 보이는 희귀한 길잃은새로, 겨울에는 대개 흰죽지나 댕기흰죽지 무리에 섞여 있다. 전국에서 관찰되지만 어디서나 수가 적어, 지금까지 한곳에서 본 가장 큰 무리도 5마리뿐이며 금강 하구와 만경강 하구에 찾아온 기록이 있다. 잠수하는 오리이지만 먹이와 습성은 잘 밝혀지지 않았다. 중국 동북부와 러시아 극동에서 번식하고 일본, 중국 남부에서 겨울을 나며, 동남아시아 북부에도 겨울에 드물게 찾아간다.

sexes.male: 머리에 녹색 광택이 돌고 가슴은 적갈색이다.

art.subject: Baer's Pochard (Aythya baeri), adult male in winter, as seen in Korea from November to March: head and upper neck blackish with a green gloss in good light; breast dark chestnut-brown; mantle and wings blackish-brown; flanks chestnut-brown with a white patch at the front of the flanks just behind the breast, showing above the waterline; belly white; undertail coverts conspicuous white; iris white; bill dark slate-grey with a black nail; legs grey.
art.pose: swimming on a reservoir among a flock of other diving ducks
art.scene: Korean winter estuary with wide open water; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view swimming: green-glossed blackish head, dark chestnut breast, chestnut-brown flanks with a white patch at the front, blackish back, white undertail coverts, white iris, grey bill
adult female, side view swimming: dark chestnut-brown head and breast, dark brown iris, brown flanks, blackish-brown back, white undertail coverts, grey bill
art.build: Medium-sized diving duck, about 45cm, the size of a Tufted Duck and noticeably smaller than a Mallard, with a rounded head and no tuft. Bill broad, grey, a little shorter than the head. Legs short, grey, set far back. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail base. Tail short, held low on the water. In flight a broad white wing-bar along the secondaries and inner primaries and a white belly.
avoid: Do not give it a crest or tuft (Tufted Duck, Aythya fuligula), and do not paint the whole flank white.
Do not paint a uniformly chestnut head on the male; his head is blackish with a green gloss (all-chestnut is Ferruginous Duck).
Do not paint a white or yellow iris on the female; only the male has a white eye.
Do not paint a grey vermiculated back (Common Pochard).
